remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive. "#31" on verso of mount is Downtown Gallery inventory number. The relationship of this series to Rodin's watercolors of similar subject, which O'Keeffe first saw in 1908 in an exhibition at 291 and again in reproduction in *Camera Work* 34–35 (April – July 1911), has been frequently noted in the literature. That the works might be self–portraits has been suggested by Sarah Whitaker Peters in *Becoming O'Keeffe* (1991) pp. 109–12, nn. 97, 99, p. 327, Barbara Rose further qualifies this idea by indicating that the nudes "are probably self–portraits in a mirror" (O'Keeffe's Originality," in *Georgia O'Keeffe Museum* [1997], p. 102. The concept is confirmed on the basis of Stieglitz–O'Keeffe correspondence. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

credit_line: Gift of The Georgia O'Keeffe Foundation
description: Vertical watercolor of seated female nude on cream background.  Seated with leg resting on other.  Body leans in bluish ground. Left across stomach below breasts into bluish ground. Face has shadow and hair is a bluish color. Body rests on blue ground. Source of light comes from the front in areas of body.   Nude No. I.  Possibly Self-Portraits etc. as noted in #176.
